name: Creator brief
summary: A brand marketer gets one brief per creator for a campaign: the product statements the brand has cleared, word for word, the disclosure that creator's platform needs, their own code and link, the dates and the review round. Nothing reaches a creator until a person reads it and sends it.

sources.title: The creator brief in Fully Powered AI's Influencer Marketing set (Fully-Powered-AI/influencer-marketing, MIT), with its rules for prepared work: only cleared statements, every gap marked for the person who supplies it, and a person who reads and sends.

sources.contribution: The parts a creator brief covers (key messages, what not to say, deliverables, creative freedom, timeline, review, disclosure, contact) and the principle that a brief guides rather than scripts.

The purpose in one sentence, a small ceiling on talking points, a call to action with the creator's own code and link, guardrails, an explicit grant of creative freedom, and where a disclosure has to sit to count, with the tags that do not count on their own.
The point that an image or demonstration can claim what the words may not, and that each claim is tied to the exact product shown.
The checks made on creator content before it is used: no competitor products, nothing inappropriate, no misleading claims. They underlie the brief's lines on competitors and redlines.
